caption:
Georgetown buyer? Skip one step and you could inherit a hidden problem.

Buying your first home in Georgetown or Halton Hills? Save this before you start. 1) Talk to a mortgage lender before you shop, so you know your real budget. 2) Count property tax, insurance and closing costs on top of the price. 3) Visit the neighbourhood on a weeknight and on a weekend. 4) Think hard before giving up your home inspection to win. 5) Plan your monthly budget for life after you move in.

caption:
Signing a Halton or Peel new build? The page you skip may cost you.

Thinking about a new-build home? Ask the builder these five questions first. 1) What is the closing date, and what happens if it moves? 2) What is included in the price, and what costs extra? 3) How much is the deposit, and when is each part due? 4) What closing costs and fees get added at the end? 5) What does the builder's warranty cover, and for how long? Get the answers in writing.

caption:
Milton buyer, approved? The real monthly bill could shock you.

Most first-time buyers look at one number, the monthly mortgage. Owning a home also means: 1) property tax, 2) home insurance, 3) heat, hydro and water, 4) repairs. Add these up before you decide what you can afford. A home that fits your monthly mortgage but not your full monthly budget can feel tight fast.

caption:
Waterloo Region buyer? Move in 2 years and it may cost you far more than you expect.

The first question to ask before buying: how long will I really stay? When you buy and later sell, there are one-time costs on both sides, like land transfer tax, legal fees and realtor fees. On a short stay, those costs have little time to pay off. If you might move in about two years, talk it through before you sign.
